pce.note: YoY derived from the PCE index stream the way Truflation defines it: index vs 365 days earlier.

source.name: Truflation US Inflation Index
source.cadence: read daily at 07:30 ET (Truflation posts new data at 23:00 UTC with a 24-hour hold)

nowcast_next_print.note: Nowflation CPI Forecast = the error-weighted blend on /forecast; in-house = the bottom-up model alone.

variants.cpi_comparable: Nowflation CPI Gauge — the CPI basket and BLS weights with live inputs where they lead (market rents for both shelter weights, AAA pump prices, Manheim used-car prices)
variants.cpi_tracker: CPI-Tracker — the same engine with the official BLS shelter indexes, so it re-tracks the print instead of leading it

official.note: CPI-U all items, NSA, YoY at one decimal exactly as BLS quotes it; each month tagged with its BLS release date.

graded.method: Same method for all rows: the reading dated the day before each BLS release (Truflation: the stream value stamped that day; Nowflation: the engine’s daily headline for that day; naive: the previous print, the last BLS YoY anyone held on print eve) against the release’s headline YoY on the NSA index at one decimal, exactly as BLS quotes it. Reference month = the month before the release month; one release per calendar month (the seasonal-factor revision date is not a print). mean_gap is signed (reading − print), sd_gap its sample standard deviation, mae the mean absolute gap, corr the Pearson r of readings against prints; beats_naive counts the prints where the reading was closer to the print than the previous print was (ties to the naive), dir_hit the share of moved prints where the reading sat on the side the print moved to. Lead test: each series’ calendar-month average (complete months only) against official YoY k months later.
graded.caveat: The CPI Gauge’s daily history is the engine’s publication-dated series (method v1.4 through the day before 2026-09-28, v1.5 from it, the level linked at the switch), not frozen daily vintages; Truflation’s is the stream as read today. Neither is a pre-registered forecast of the print — the graded receipts for that live on /scoreboard.

bls.label: No clean BLS equivalent ingested

truflation.note: Category YoYs and the +2.0% headline are from Truflation’s July-2026 report; weights from their 2026 weights note. The headline is the month’s average of the daily index; the weighted sum of the one-decimal category YoYs lands a few tenths higher, which is rounding plus the difference between a monthly average and the categories’ own reference timing.

bls.note: Weights are the BLS CPI-U relative-importance values the engine uses for the year (renormalized); the residual is the unmapped part of the basket (transportation services, household furnishings, alcohol & tobacco, personal care, other services).

nowflation.note: Component YoYs from the engine’s daily component indexes on the last day of the report month (base variant), weights for the year; the residual is index-aggregation rounding.

truflation.concept: A cost-of-living index on a household-spending basket, published daily.
facts: Twelve categories weighted by prior-year household spending — credit-card transaction data, Census data and household-expenditure data from Global Demographics and NielsenIQ, validated against Truflation’s own feeds — against the 24-month-old expenditure survey behind the CPI weights. The 2026 weights put housing at 23.1% of the basket; shelter is about 34% of the BLS CPI-U.
Rented dwellings (8.1% of the basket): five sources equally weighted — Numbeo, Penn State ACY, Zillow, Redfin and Apartment List.

Owned dwellings (13.7%): a cost-of-ownership calculation — property values, new-mortgage rates from Freddie Mac blended into the existing mortgage stock, property taxes, maintenance and insurance — rather than the BLS owners’-equivalent-rent imputation.
Health (8.8%) includes health-insurance premiums at a 6.2% weight; transportation (19.8%) carries vehicle insurance at 3.2%.
Monthly sources are carried forward daily; the index is based 2010-01-01 = 100 and YoY is the index against its value 365 days earlier. New data posts at 23:00 UTC with a 24-hour hold.

Truflation’s own lead estimate: its US index leads the BLS print by about 45 days, with a correlation of 0.83 in the current regime (Truflation, “Truflation as a Leading Indicator of the Official US Inflation”, February 2026 — https://truflation.com/blog/truflation-leading-indicator-of-us-cpi).

sources.label: Truflation US monthly inflation report — July 2026

nowflation.concept: What would the CPI print if its inputs were read today? The CPI basket and BLS weights with live inputs where they lead, graded against the print.
facts: 21 components on the BLS CPI-U relative-importance weights (shelter about a third of the basket), each a publication-dated daily index built from its BLS subindex, with a live input spliced on where one has a better record: the all-tenant rent model (new-lease rents from Zillow ZORI and Apartment List, rolled over at the pace of the CPI's rent panel) on both the rent and owners'-equivalent weights, AAA's daily pump price for motor fuel, Manheim's used-vehicle value index, and Kelley Blue Book's average transaction price for new vehicles; from method v1.5 a monthly source steps aside for the official subindex while the BLS has published a newer month.

A component without a live input rides its latest official subindex between prints. Year over year is taken against each component's own year-ago level (for a held component, the same month's print a year earlier), not against the index value 365 days before.
The CPI Gauge is the CPI-comparable reading that feeds the Nowflation Forecast; Nowflation Realtime is the site's headline measurement of prices today.

Every reading is stored with the date it was pulled, the daily history is dated on the publication calendar (method v1.5 since 2026-09-28, v1.4 before), and the next-print forecast is pre-registered and graded on /scoreboard.
